This report evaluates the reliability of the focal psychometric item sets in
`Res_2_Data_for_Analysis/dat_focal_analysis.rda`, the canonical analysis-entry
file created by S1.2.

Baseline reliability is estimated at the participant level using Cronbach's
alpha and McDonald's omega from the `psych` package. EMA reliability is
estimated at the prompt-within-person and person-between levels using
`multilevelTools::omegaSEM()`. The CRAN package named `multilevel` does not
provide a multilevel omega function; `omegaSEM()` is implemented in
`multilevelTools`.

The EMA analyses cover the six-item PSMU and Psychological Distress item sets,
the Core and Peripheral PSMU subdimensions, and the three two-item Psychological
Distress subdomains: Depressive symptoms, Anxiety symptoms, and Perceived stress.
All seven item sets are included in the final reliability summary.

No scale total, scale mean, daily aggregate, or new analysis RDA is created by
this report.

# Helper functions

```{r helpers}
run_baseline_reliability <- function(data, scale_name, items) {
  item_data <- data[, items, drop = FALSE]
  n_complete <- sum(stats::complete.cases(item_data))

  alpha_fit <- psych::alpha(
    item_data,
    check.keys = FALSE,
    warnings = FALSE,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  omega_fit <- suppressWarnings(
    psych::omega(
      item_data,
      nfactors = 1,
      plot = FALSE,
      title = scale_name
    )
  )

  summary <- data.frame(
    scale = scale_name,
    items = length(items),
    participants = nrow(item_data),
    complete_cases = n_complete,
    cronbach_alpha_raw = alpha_fit$total$raw_alpha,
    cronbach_alpha_standardized = alpha_fit$total$std.alpha,
    guttman_lambda_6 = alpha_fit$total[["G6(smc)"]],
    average_interitem_correlation = alpha_fit$total$average_r,
    mcdonald_omega_total = omega_fit$omega.tot,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  alpha_if_deleted <- data.frame(
    scale = scale_name,
    item_deleted = rownames(alpha_fit$alpha.drop),
    alpha_raw_if_deleted = alpha_fit$alpha.drop$raw_alpha,
    alpha_standardized_if_deleted = alpha_fit$alpha.drop$std.alpha,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    row.names = NULL
  )

  list(summary = summary, alpha_if_deleted = alpha_if_deleted)
}

run_multilevel_omega <- function(data, scale_name, items, require_saturated = FALSE) {
  complete_rows <- stats::complete.cases(data[, c("Name_ID", items), drop = FALSE])
  n_complete_prompts <- sum(complete_rows)
  n_complete_people <- dplyr::n_distinct(data$Name_ID[complete_rows])

  omega_fit <- multilevelTools::omegaSEM(
    items = items,
    id = "Name_ID",
    data = data,
    savemodel = TRUE
  )

  if (!isTRUE(lavaan::lavInspect(omega_fit$Fit, "converged"))) {
    stop("Multilevel omega model did not converge for: ", scale_name)
  }

  # Retain the original two-item diagnostic internally; do not report fit indices.
  if (isTRUE(require_saturated)) {
    model_df <- unname(lavaan::fitMeasures(omega_fit$Fit, "df"))
    if (!isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(model_df), 0))) {
      stop("Expected a saturated two-item model for: ", scale_name)
    }
  }

  reliability <- omega_fit$Results |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      scale = scale_name,
      level = dplyr::recode(label, omega_within = "Within person", omega_between = "Between person"),
      omega = est,
      ci_lower = ci.lower,
      ci_upper = ci.upper,
      items = length(items),
      complete_prompts = n_complete_prompts,
      participants_with_complete_prompt = n_complete_people
    )

  list(reliability = reliability, model = omega_fit$Fit)
}
```

# Baseline

Baseline variables are repeated across EMA prompts in the analysis-entry file.
They are therefore reduced to one verified-constant row per participant before
reliability estimation.

## Prepare participant-level item data

PSS items 4, 5, 7, and 8 are reverse-keyed in the focal-variable Word document.
The observed response range is 1-5, so the temporary reliability copy applies
`6 - x`. These recoded values are used only within S1.3 and are not written back
to `dat_focal_analysis.rda`.

```{r baseline-preparation}
baseline_item_names <- unique(unlist(baseline_scale_items))

baseline_constancy <- vapply(
  baseline_item_names,
  function(variable) {
    max(vapply(
      split(dat_focal_analysis[[variable]], dat_focal_analysis$Name_ID),
      function(x) length(unique(x[!is.na(x)])),
      integer(1)
    ))
  },
  integer(1)
)
if (any(baseline_constancy > 1L)) {
  stop("Baseline items vary within participant: ", paste(names(baseline_constancy)[baseline_constancy > 1L], collapse = ", "))
}

dat_baseline_reliability <- dat_focal_analysis |>
  dplyr::distinct(Name_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(Name_ID, dplyr::all_of(baseline_item_names)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID)

pss_reverse_items <- baseline_reverse_keys[["Perceived stress (PSS-10)"]]
dat_baseline_reliability <- dat_baseline_reliability |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(pss_reverse_items), ~ 6 - .x))

stopifnot(
  nrow(dat_baseline_reliability) == 209L,
  dplyr::n_distinct(dat_baseline_reliability$Name_ID) == 209L
)

data.frame(
  participants = nrow(dat_baseline_reliability),
  baseline_items = length(baseline_item_names),
  reverse_scored_for_reliability = paste(pss_reverse_items, collapse = ", "),
  saved_to_analysis_rda = "No",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline preparation",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

## Cronbach alpha and McDonald omega

McDonald's omega is estimated as a one-factor omega total for each prespecified
item set. The result should be interpreted together with the construct's known
content structure rather than as proof of unidimensionality.

```{r baseline-reliability}
baseline_reliability_objects <- lapply(names(baseline_scale_items), function(scale_name) {
  run_baseline_reliability(
    data = dat_baseline_reliability,
    scale_name = scale_name,
    items = baseline_scale_items[[scale_name]]
  )
})

baseline_reliability_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(baseline_reliability_objects, `[[`, "summary")
)

baseline_alpha_if_deleted <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(baseline_reliability_objects, `[[`, "alpha_if_deleted")
)

baseline_reliability_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline reliability",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

# EMA

EMA data remain at the prompt level, with prompts nested within `Name_ID`.
Multilevel omega is estimated separately at the within-person and between-person
levels using a two-level single-factor SEM for each item set.

The models use the original 1-5 item responses as continuous indicators. The
`omegaSEM()` function delegates estimation to `lavaan::sem()` with ML and
listwise missing-data handling, so each model uses prompts complete on its own
item set. It fixes the factor variance to one at each level and constrains
item residual variances to be positive. Reported 95% confidence intervals use
the default normal-theory intervals for the defined omega parameters.

The use-time and use-frequency variables represent distinct behavior categories
(messaging, posting, and browsing), not exchangeable indicators of a single
reflective construct, so internal-consistency reliability is not estimated for
them.

## Multilevel omega

```{r ema-multilevel-omega}
ema_reliability_objects <- lapply(names(ema_scale_items), function(scale_name) {
  run_multilevel_omega(
    data = dat_focal_analysis,
    scale_name = scale_name,
    items = ema_scale_items[[scale_name]]
  )
})

ema_multilevel_omega <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(ema_reliability_objects, `[[`, "reliability")
)

ema_multilevel_omega |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Multilevel omega for EMA PSMU and Psychological Distress",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

## Multilevel Omegas for Core and Peripheral PSMU Symptoms

Core comprises PMU3 mood modification, PMU4 relapse, PMU5 withdrawal, and PMU6
conflict. Peripheral comprises PMU1 salience and PMU2 tolerance. These are
prespecified groups of state manifestations. The same `run_multilevel_omega()`
helper used for the total scales estimates each subdimension directly from the
canonical prompt-level item data, without constructing scores or daily means.

```{r ema-psmu-subdimension-specifications}
data.frame(
  subdimension = names(ema_psmu_subdimension_items),
  items = vapply(ema_psmu_subdimension_items, paste, collapse = ", ", character(1)),
  item_count = lengths(ema_psmu_subdimension_items),
  method = "multilevelTools::omegaSEM()",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Core and Peripheral PSMU subdimension specifications",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

```{r ema-psmu-subdimension-omega}
ema_psmu_subdimension_objects <- lapply(names(ema_psmu_subdimension_items), function(subdimension_name) {
  items <- ema_psmu_subdimension_items[[subdimension_name]]
  run_multilevel_omega(
    data = dat_focal_analysis,
    scale_name = subdimension_name,
    items = items,
    require_saturated = length(items) == 2L
  )
})

ema_psmu_subdimension_omega <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(ema_psmu_subdimension_objects, `[[`, "reliability")
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(ema_psmu_subdimension_omega) == 4L,
  all(ema_psmu_subdimension_omega$participants_with_complete_prompt == 209L),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(ema_psmu_subdimension_omega[c("omega", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")]))),
  all(ema_psmu_subdimension_omega$ci_lower <= ema_psmu_subdimension_omega$omega),
  all(ema_psmu_subdimension_omega$omega <= ema_psmu_subdimension_omega$ci_upper)
)

ema_psmu_subdimension_omega |>
  dplyr::select(
    subdimension = scale, level, items, complete_prompts,
    participants_with_complete_prompt, omega, ci_lower, ci_upper
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Multilevel omega and 95% confidence intervals for Core and Peripheral PSMU symptoms",
    col.names = c("Subdimension", "Level", "Items", "Complete prompts", "Participants", "Omega", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper"),
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

For Peripheral, `omegaSEM()` identifies the two-item model by constraining its
loadings equal separately at the within-person and between-person levels. This
essential tau-equivalence assumption is not tested by the saturated model.
Core's four loadings are freely estimated at each level. High omega alone does
not establish unidimensionality or a formal Core-versus-Peripheral difference.

## Multilevel Omegas for EMA Psychological Distress Subdomains

The three prespecified two-item subdomains retain the same item grouping and
estimation settings as the total-scale analyses. No domain score is created:
each model receives the canonical prompt-level item data with missing values
retained and prompts nested within `Name_ID`. The reported complete-prompt
counts describe each model's own listwise-complete estimation sample.

```{r ema-distress-subdomain-specifications}
data.frame(
  subdomain = names(ema_distress_subdomain_items),
  items = vapply(ema_distress_subdomain_items, paste, collapse = ", ", character(1)),
  item_count = lengths(ema_distress_subdomain_items),
  method = "multilevelTools::omegaSEM()",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "EMA Psychological Distress subdomain specifications",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

```{r ema-distress-subdomain-omega}
ema_distress_subdomain_objects <- lapply(names(ema_distress_subdomain_items), function(subdomain_name) {
  run_multilevel_omega(
    data = dat_focal_analysis,
    scale_name = subdomain_name,
    items = ema_distress_subdomain_items[[subdomain_name]],
    require_saturated = TRUE
  )
})

ema_distress_subdomain_omega <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(ema_distress_subdomain_objects, `[[`, "reliability")
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(ema_distress_subdomain_omega) == 6L,
  all(ema_distress_subdomain_omega$participants_with_complete_prompt == 209L),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(ema_distress_subdomain_omega[c("omega", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")]))),
  all(ema_distress_subdomain_omega$ci_lower <= ema_distress_subdomain_omega$omega),
  all(ema_distress_subdomain_omega$omega <= ema_distress_subdomain_omega$ci_upper)
)

ema_distress_subdomain_omega |>
  dplyr::select(
    subdomain = scale, level, items, complete_prompts,
    participants_with_complete_prompt, omega, ci_lower, ci_upper
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Multilevel omega and 95% confidence intervals for EMA Psychological Distress subdomains",
    col.names = c("Subdomain", "Level", "Items", "Complete prompts", "Participants", "Omega", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper"),
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

Each subdomain has only two items, with loadings constrained equal separately
at each level, and a saturated two-level model. Its omega
estimates summarize reliability; they do not establish unidimensionality or
measurement-model adequacy. Convergence and the expected saturation are checked
in code, without a model-fit table.

Within-person omega concerns occasion-to-occasion variation within participants;
between-person omega concerns differences in participants' average levels and
should not be interpreted as single-prompt reliability. All 209 participants
contribute at least one complete prompt to each subdomain. Some participants
have no within-person variation on individual items; this does not imply that
they were excluded, but warrants interpreting reliability alongside the item
distributions.

# Reliability Summary

Baseline reliability is reported for four participant-level item sets. The EMA
summary covers both six-item total scales, Core and Peripheral PSMU, and all
three two-item Psychological Distress subdomains, with separate within-person
and between-person estimates (14 coefficients across seven item sets).
High reliability alone does not demonstrate a single underlying dimension.

## Baseline reliability

```{r final-summary}
baseline_reliability_summary |>
  dplyr::select(
    scale,
    items,
    participants,
    complete_cases,
    cronbach_alpha = cronbach_alpha_raw,
    mcdonald_omega = mcdonald_omega_total
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline reliability summary",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

# Excel results

The tables above are exported to
`Res_3_Results/Table_S1_3_Reliability.xlsx`. The two sheets are `Baseline`
(scale reliability and alpha if item deleted) and `EMA` (the two total scales,
Core and Peripheral PSMU, and three distress subdomains; 14 level-specific rows).
No measurement-model fit table is exported.
Numeric estimates retain their available precision; Excel formats control
display rounding. `write_artifacts: false` disables only file writes, not the
analyses earlier in this report.

```{r export-excel}
if (isTRUE(params$write_artifacts)) {
  # Retain an existing report's layout when its baseline results are unchanged.
  # A fresh checkout falls through to the self-contained workbook export below.
  update_existing_ema <- function(path, baseline, item_deleted, ema) {
    if (!file.exists(path)) return(FALSE)
    same_values <- function(x, y) {
      identical(dim(x), dim(y)) && all(vapply(seq_len(ncol(x)), function(j) {
        isTRUE(all.equal(x[[j]], y[[j]], tolerance = 0, check.attributes = FALSE))
      }, logical(1)))
    }
    read_block <- function(sheet, range) as.data.frame(readxl::read_xlsx(
      path, sheet = sheet, range = range, .name_repair = "minimal"))
    compatible <- tryCatch(
      identical(readxl::excel_sheets(path), c("Baseline", "EMA")) &&
        same_values(read_block("Baseline", "A5:I9"), baseline) &&
        same_values(read_block("Baseline", "A12:D54"), item_deleted) &&
        identical(names(read_block("EMA", "A5:H9")), c(
          "Scale", "Level", "Items", "Complete prompts", "Participants",
          "Omega", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper")),
      error = function(e) FALSE)
    if (!compatible) return(FALSE)
    scratch <- tempfile("s1_3_excel_")
    dir.create(scratch)
    on.exit(unlink(scratch, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
    members <- utils::unzip(path, list = TRUE)$Name
    stopifnot(!any(grepl("(^/|^[A-Za-z]:|(^|/)\\.\\.(/|$)|\\\\)", members)))
    utils::unzip(path, exdir = scratch)
    worksheet <- file.path(scratch, "xl/worksheets/sheet2.xml")
    doc <- xml2::read_xml(worksheet)
    ns <- c(x = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main")
    rows <- xml2::xml_find_first(doc, ".//x:sheetData", ns)
    template <- xml2::xml_find_first(rows, "x:row[@r='9']", ns)
    stopifnot(!inherits(template, "xml_missing"), nrow(ema) == 14L, ncol(ema) == 8L)
    if (length(xml2::xml_find_all(template, "x:c[@t='str']", ns)) != 2L) return(FALSE)
    # Preserve total-scale values; synchronize their labels with the report.
    old_ema <- read_block("EMA", "A5:H9")
    if (!same_values(old_ema[-1L], ema[1:4, -1L])) return(FALSE)
    for (index in seq_len(4L)) {
      label_cell <- xml2::xml_find_first(rows, paste0(
        "x:row/x:c[@r='A", index + 5L, "']/x:v"), ns)
      stopifnot(!inherits(label_cell, "xml_missing"))
      xml2::xml_text(label_cell) <- as.character(ema[[1L]][index])
    }
    xml2::xml_remove(xml2::xml_find_all(rows, "x:row[number(@r) >= 10]", ns))
    merges <- xml2::xml_find_all(doc, ".//x:mergeCells/x:mergeCell", ns)
    for (merge in merges) {
      span <- strsplit(xml2::xml_attr(merge, "ref"), ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
      if (max(as.integer(gsub("[A-Z]", "", span))) >= 10L) xml2::xml_remove(merge)
    }
    merge_parent <- xml2::xml_find_first(doc, ".//x:mergeCells", ns)
    if (!inherits(merge_parent, "xml_missing")) {
      xml2::xml_set_attr(merge_parent, "count", length(xml2::xml_children(merge_parent)))
    }
    for (index in seq.int(5L, nrow(ema))) {
      row_number <- index + 5L
      row <- xml2::xml_add_child(rows, template, .copy = TRUE)
      xml2::xml_set_attr(row, "r", row_number)
      cells <- xml2::xml_find_all(row, "x:c", ns)
      stopifnot(length(cells) == 8L)
      for (column in seq_len(8L)) {
        cell <- cells[[column]]
        xml2::xml_set_attr(cell, "r", paste0(LETTERS[column], row_number))
        value <- ema[[column]][index]
        if (column <= 2L) {
          target <- xml2::xml_find_first(cell, "x:v", ns)
          stopifnot(!inherits(target, "xml_missing"), !is.na(value))
          xml2::xml_text(target) <- as.character(value)
        } else {
          target <- xml2::xml_find_first(cell, "x:v", ns)
          stopifnot(!inherits(target, "xml_missing"), is.finite(value))
          xml2::xml_text(target) <- sprintf("%.17g", value)
        }
      }
    }
    dimension <- xml2::xml_find_first(doc, ".//x:dimension", ns)
    if (!inherits(dimension, "xml_missing")) {
      xml2::xml_set_attr(dimension, "ref", paste0("A1:H", nrow(ema) + 5L))
    }
    xml2::write_xml(doc, worksheet)
    candidate <- file.path(scratch, "updated.xlsx")
    zip::zipr(candidate, files = members, root = scratch,
              include_directories = FALSE, mode = "mirror")
    reloaded <- as.data.frame(readxl::read_xlsx(candidate, sheet = "EMA",
      range = paste0("A5:H", nrow(ema) + 5L), .name_repair = "minimal"))
    stopifnot(same_values(reloaded, ema), file.info(candidate)$size > 1000,
              file.copy(candidate, path, overwrite = TRUE))
    TRUE
  }
  ema_export <- ema_reliability_summary[c("scale", "level", "items", "complete_prompts",
    "participants_with_complete_prompt", "omega", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")]
  if (!update_existing_ema(excel_output, baseline_reliability_summary,
                          baseline_alpha_if_deleted, ema_export)) {
  normalize_openxml_relationships <- function(path) {
    # Remove only worksheet drawing/VML relationships whose internal targets
    # are absent. Preserve valid drawings, external links and all other parts.
    unpack_dir <- tempfile("s1_3_xlsx_")
    dir.create(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    on.exit(unlink(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE), add = TRUE)

    members <- utils::unzip(path, list = TRUE)$Name
    unsafe_member <- function(member) {
      parts <- strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "/", member), "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
      grepl("^[/\\\\]|^[A-Za-z]:", member) || any(parts == "..")
    }
    stopifnot(length(members) > 0L, !anyDuplicated(members),
              !any(vapply(members, unsafe_member, logical(1))))
    utils::unzip(path, exdir = unpack_dir)
    relationship_files <- list.files(
      file.path(unpack_dir, "xl", "worksheets", "_rels"),
      pattern = "[.]rels$", full.names = TRUE
    )
    if (!length(relationship_files)) return(invisible(path))

    resolve_member <- function(target) {
      target <- gsub("\\\\", "/", utils::URLdecode(target))
      if (!nzchar(target) || grepl("^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:", target)) {
        stop("Invalid internal drawing target")
      }
      parts <- strsplit(target, "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
      result <- if (startsWith(target, "/")) character() else c("xl", "worksheets")
      for (part in parts) {
        if (!nzchar(part) || part == ".") next
        if (part == "..") {
          if (!length(result)) stop("Drawing target escapes the workbook package")
          result <- head(result, -1L)
        } else result <- c(result, part)
      }
      paste(result, collapse = "/")
    }
    drawing_types <- paste0(
      "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/",
      c("drawing", "vmlDrawing")
    )
    removed_relationships <- 0L
    for (relationship_file in relationship_files) {
      document <- xml2::read_xml(relationship_file, options = "NONET")
      relationships <- xml2::xml_find_all(
        document, "/*[local-name()='Relationships']/*[local-name()='Relationship']"
      )
      changed <- FALSE
      for (relationship in relationships) {
        type <- xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "Type")
        external <- identical(xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "TargetMode"), "External")
        if (!type %in% drawing_types || external) next
        target <- xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "Target")
        if (is.na(target)) stop("Drawing relationship is missing its Target")
        if (!resolve_member(target) %in% members) {
          xml2::xml_remove(relationship)
          removed_relationships <- removed_relationships + 1L
          changed <- TRUE
        }
      }
      if (changed) xml2::write_xml(document, relationship_file)
    }
    if (removed_relationships == 0L) return(invisible(path))

    normalized_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
    on.exit(unlink(normalized_file, force = TRUE), add = TRUE)
    zip::zipr(
      normalized_file,
      files = list.files(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE),
      root = unpack_dir,
      include_directories = FALSE,
      mode = "mirror"
    )
    if (!file.copy(normalized_file, path, overwrite = TRUE)) {
      stop("Could not replace the workbook with its normalized OpenXML package.")
    }
    unlink(normalized_file, force = TRUE)
    invisible(path)
  }

  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook(creator = "Kunru Song")
  header_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", wrapText = TRUE)
  decimal_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(numFmt = "0.000")
  integer_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(numFmt = "0")

  write_result_section <- function(sheet, title, data, headers, start_row,
                                   integer_columns = integer()) {
    stopifnot(is.data.frame(data), ncol(data) == length(headers))
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet, title, startRow = start_row, colNames = FALSE)
    names(data) <- headers
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet, data, startRow = start_row + 1L,
                        rowNames = FALSE, headerStyle = header_style, keepNA = TRUE)
    if (nrow(data)) {
      rows <- seq.int(start_row + 2L, length.out = nrow(data))
      numeric_columns <- which(vapply(data, is.numeric, logical(1)))
      for (column in numeric_columns) {
        openxlsx::addStyle(wb, sheet,
          if (column %in% integer_columns) integer_style else decimal_style,
          rows = rows, cols = column, gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE)
      }
    }
    start_row + nrow(data) + 4L
  }

  for (sheet in c("Baseline", "EMA")) {
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sheet, gridLines = FALSE)
    openxlsx::freezePane(wb, sheet, firstActiveRow = 3L)
  }
  next_row <- write_result_section("Baseline", "Baseline reliability",
    baseline_reliability_summary,
    c("Scale", "Items", "N", "Complete N", "Cronbach alpha", "Standardized alpha",
      "Guttman lambda 6", "Average inter-item r", "McDonald omega"), 1L, 2:4)
  write_result_section("Baseline", "Alpha if item deleted", baseline_alpha_if_deleted,
    c("Scale", "Item deleted", "Raw alpha if deleted", "Standardized alpha if deleted"),
    next_row)
  write_result_section("EMA", "EMA multilevel reliability",
    ema_reliability_summary[c("scale", "level", "items", "complete_prompts",
      "participants_with_complete_prompt", "omega", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")],
    c("Scale", "Level", "Items", "Complete prompts", "Participants", "Omega",
      "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper"), 1L, 3:5)
  for (sheet in c("Baseline", "EMA")) {
    openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, sheet, cols = 1L, widths = 46)
    openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, sheet, cols = 2:9, widths = 22)
  }
  dir.create(dirname(excel_output), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, excel_output, overwrite = TRUE)
  normalize_openxml_relationships(excel_output)
  }
}
```
